content.overview: BNS s. 234 — Issuing or signing false certificate.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Issuing or signing false certificate. BNS restatement of IPC 198. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 198. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 234 is the rule on “Issuing or signing false certificate”. The section provides that whoever issues or signs any certificate required by law to be given or signed, or relating to any fact of which such certificate is by law admissible in evidence, knowing or believing that such certificate is false in any material point, shall be punished in the same manner as if he gave false evidence. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 234 exists so that “Issuing or signing false certificate” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.

The provision in detail
234.
